correctness.rationale: Riemann–Hurwitz gives 2g−2=−2p+4(p−1). Descending through the invariant rational function field sends the marked deck normalizer into V₄ with kernel H. A permutation of the branch points lifts exactly when it preserves the Kummer valuations modulo p up to a common nonzero scalar; a divisor divisible by p is a pth power up to constant on the complex projective line, proving sufficiency. Every nonidentity base permutation is a double transposition, so the scalar squares to 1. The +1 case pairs equal entries and zero sum forces repeated opposites. The −1 case pairs opposite entries, giving one such pairing for four distinct entries and two in the repeated case. Thus the three quotient/action possibilities are trivial, C₂ acting by inversion, and V₄ with a sign map of kernel C₂. Coprimality splits the extensions, giving the claimed groups. The distinct-pair type is parametrized by the nonidentity inversion orbits of F_p^×/{±1}, of which there are floor((p−1)/4). Subtracting from the known total gives the remainder. Independently, on the projective nonzero zero-sum tuples for p≥5, fixed-point counts for the five S₄ conjugacy types (identity, transposition, double transposition, 3-cycle, 4-cycle) are p²−3p+3, p−2, p, 1, and 1+2·1_(p≡1 mod 4), respectively; Burnside agrees with Table 10. For p=3 zero sum forces exactly two entries of each sign, so only the first type occurs. Bounded independent enumeration at /workspace/branches/69b9ab1d-e09b-447b-bdd5-c90f1341b254/record5_reproduction.py matches the counts through p=41; it tests monodromy orbits and liftability, not complex curve automorphisms beyond the normalizer. The uploaded verify.py was inspected, not run.
